topic: palo alto pan-os cve security vulnerability
headline_marked: Palo Alto Networks: [[CVE-2026-0321 allows unauthenticated DoS]] on PAN-OS dataplanes
headline: Palo Alto Networks: CVE-2026-0321 allows unauthenticated DoS on PAN-OS dataplanes
summary: Unlike other recent PAN-OS vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-0321 enables a denial-of-service condition via crafted network traffic without requiring any attacker credentials. This makes it a critical priority.
details: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed CVE-2026-0321, a critical denial-of-service vulnerability affecting PAN-OS dataplanes. An unauthenticated attacker with network access can send crafted traffic, leading to a DoS condition and potentially forcing the device into maintenance mode. This flaw stands out from other recent advisories due to its lack of authentication requirement.

While the CVSS 4.0 base score is a MEDIUM 6.6, this rating reflects impact dimensions rather than attacker effort. Many other vulnerabilities in the October 2026 batch, such as CVE-2026-0316 or CVE-2026-0322, require authenticated administrator access or local privileges. CVE-2026-0321's unauthenticated nature makes it significantly easier to exploit.

Organizations are advised to prioritize patching for CVE-2026-0321 separately from other authenticated issues. Its blast radius targets network traffic directly, not credentials, necessitating a shorter deadline for remediation. Cloud NGFW and Panorama are unaffected by this specific CVE, though Panorama has its own separate vulnerability (CVE-2026-0318).

The vulnerability impacts PAN-OS versions 10.2 through 12.2 branches, with specific hotfix lines for each. Enterprises running PAN-OS dataplanes at their perimeter should treat this as an urgent matter. A ZoomEye search on October 22, 2026, showed over 22,000 Palo Alto Networks assets, though specific vulnerable devices are not yet indexed.

topic: cloudflare workers ai free tier pricing
headline_marked: Cloudflare Workers AI offers [[10,000 free Neurons daily]], then $0.011 per 1,000
headline: Cloudflare Workers AI offers 10,000 free Neurons daily, then $0.011 per 1,000
summary: Cloudflare Workers AI provides 10,000 Neurons free per day, resetting at 00:00 UTC. Exceeding this requires a Workers Paid plan, costing $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons beyond the free tier.
details: Cloudflare Workers AI now grants every account 10,000 free Neurons daily, resetting at 00:00 UTC. For usage beyond this, the cost is $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons on the Workers Paid plan. This amounts to 300,000 free Neurons over a 30-day month.

Workers Free accounts receive the same daily 10,000 Neurons. To go past this allocation, users must upgrade to a Workers Paid plan, which has a $5 per month minimum charge. Some models also support prepaid AI Gateway credits as an alternative.

The Neuron billing system underpins varying per-token prices, with input and output priced separately per million tokens. The difference between the cheapest and most expensive input prices can be as high as 49x. Users are advised to select the smallest model that meets their test requirements.

Rate limits apply independently of Neuron usage. Text generation is capped at 300 requests per minute, or 20-50 requests per minute for models requiring the Workers Paid plan. Other tasks like text embeddings and translation have their own limits, such as 3,000 and 720 requests per minute, respectively.

Models can be called from the fetch handler using env.AI.run. Deployment is done via npx wrangler deploy, and npx wrangler dev allows local testing. However, local runs still consume from your Cloudflare account's Neuron allocation.

All pricing information is based on Cloudflare's documentation as of October 2026. Users should always check the official Workers AI pricing page for the most current rates before committing budget, as prices are subject to change.
